instruction: Convert a LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet directly into a standalone desktop application using only Calc's built-in export features, without using any extensions, macros, terminal commands, or external tools.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened LibreOffice Impress, created a simple presentation with title and text, explored File > Export (found only static image/document formats), File > Export As (only PDF), and Slide Show menu (no video/animation export). Correctly identified the video export task as infeasible.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open applications from menu, navigate LibreOffice Impress menus, create presentation content (title/text), explore export format options, correctly identify infeasible tasks by outputting [INFEASIBLE]
metadata.task_rationale: Tests whether model can correctly identify that LibreOffice Calc cannot export to an executable/application format. Same pattern as original task (impossible export format), but in Calc instead of Impress, and targeting an even more obviously impossible output format.
metadata.challenge_additions: The model must explore Calc's export and save-as options and determine that no application/executable export exists. Calc supports many export formats (xlsx, csv, pdf, html, etc.) but none produce standalone applications.
metadata.explanation: LibreOffice Calc can export to document formats (xlsx, ods, csv, pdf, html) but has no capability to create standalone desktop applications. The model must explore Save As and Export menus in Calc and correctly identify this as infeasible.

llm_judge_reasons: The instruction asks to convert a LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet into a standalone desktop application, which is genuinely impossible using Calc's built-in features.

The 'infeasible' evaluator is the correct choice for this task — LibreOffice Calc supports only document export formats (xlsx, ods, csv, pdf, html) and has no capability to produce executables or applications.
The task follows the same proven pattern as the source trajectory (impossible export format in LibreOffice), adapted from Impress to Calc with an even more obviously impossible target format.
Complete verification coverage: the single requirement (impossible conversion) is fully captured by the infeasible evaluator.
